title: How to Define the ‘Reasonable’ in Reasonable Doubt
partialText: “Beyond a reasonable doubt” is the highest burden of proof within the American legal system. Still, there is some wiggle room.

title: A More Confident Iran Emerges After Six Months of War With the U.S.
partialText: New intelligence reports have assessed that Iran now has a far better understanding of its capabilities and the limits of U.S. power.

title: Yemen’s Houthis Push Toward Red Sea Strait as Ground Fighting Escalates
partialText: The Houthis, an Iran-backed militia, appear to be trying to gain control of a port city near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key choke point for global trade.

title: Israel Says It Is Cementing Its Foothold in Southern Lebanon
partialText: The recent capture of a strategic ridge has further entrenched the Israeli occupation of Lebanese territory, as efforts to broker lasting peace have floundered.

title: Robust Hiring Reinforces Strength of the U.S. Economy
partialText: Employers added 162,000 jobs and unemployment held at 4.1 percent last month, signs of a stability that contrasted with high inflation weighing on households and markets.

title: Trump Threatens to Halt Some Trade Unless the Fed Cuts Rates
partialText: The president said he could halt trade between the United States and countries with which it has a trade deficit if the central bank doesn’t do his bidding.

title: The Risk of Russian Sabotage in Europe: A Fight That Spirals Out of Control
partialText: Europe’s options are limited in responding to an unnerving series of plots and provocations. But the odds of unpredictable consequences are rising.

title: Kushner and Witkoff to Go to Russia and Ukraine to Revive Peace Talks
partialText: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff’s trip to meet with the countries’ presidents comes at a precarious moment in the Ukraine conflict.

title: Russian Drone Strikes Office of Ukraine’s Intelligence Chief
partialText: The attack came as the American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were said to be planning imminent visits to Kyiv and to Moscow.

title: Sandra Bullock, Nicole Kidman and the Other ‘Practical Magic 2’ Stars on the Unlikely Sequel
partialText: Sandra Bullock, Nicole Kidman, Joey King and Maisie Williams on the unlikely sequel, embracing their witchiness and their hopes for a third film.

title: Pentagon Agreement With N.I.H. on Biodefense Draws Alarm From Democrats
partialText: Under a new partnership, the Defense Department would play a larger role in biodefense and pandemic preparedness. Democrats warned it could allow a Pentagon cash grab.

title: ICE Agent Charged With Six Counts of Lying About Minnesota Shooting
partialText: The federal indictment against Christian Castro marked a rare instance of the Trump administration seeking to hold an immigration agent accountable for actions taken while on duty.

title: Trump Administration Moves to Drop Protections for More Wetlands
partialText: The proposed rule could strip federal protections from most U.S. wetlands, many of which help feed drinking water systems.

title: Corporate America Is Getting Hooked on Open-Source A.I.
partialText: Companies like AT&T are increasingly using cheap, freely available artificial intelligence models over expensive ones from Anthropic and OpenAI.

title: Why the Hugging Face Hack Should Make You Worry More About A.I.
partialText: The attack by an aggressive “collective” of OpenAI agents shows the danger of artificial intelligence systems that organize themselves.

title: ‘I Don’t Want to Die This Way’: Stranded for 15 Hours at Sea
partialText: Two longtime friends rented jet skis for an hourlong excursion. They ended up fighting for their lives.

title: The U.S. Wants the Oil From These 17 Venezuelan Fields
partialText: A private oil company has struck a deal with the Trump administration to develop 17 areas in Venezuela, an effort that experts say will take years and billions of dollars.

title: Alejandro Betancourt, Trump’s Partner in Venezuelan Oil Deal, Has Faced Investigations
partialText: Alejandro Betancourt has been targeted by multiple investigations. Now he’s the U.S. government’s unrivaled partner in President Trump’s bid to control Venezuelan oil resources.

title: Gloria Steinem Stayed Positive, Even as the Manosphere Took Hold
partialText: The feminist icon thought many women would carry on her legacy. But at an unsteady time for feminism, how will the movement carry on?

title: Gloria Steinem Found Community and Clout Over the Dinner Table
partialText: Neither a home cook nor an enthusiastic eater, she used the dinner table as a place to forge relationships and foster change.

title: Inside Mamdani’s Private Army of Public Influencers
partialText: Zohran Mamdani is seen as a social media wizard. Some of his popularity stems from an influencer operation run by the mayor’s office.

title: The Search for New Cures Is Broken
partialText: It is too hard for medical researchers to launch clinical trials.

title: To Save Gaza, Resist Hamas
partialText: If Western supporters of the Palestinians want to help Gaza, denounce Hamas.

title: Build First, Ask Later
partialText: We look at President Trump’s building spree in Washington.

title: New Yorkers: Share Your Thoughts About Israel, Gaza and Jewish Identity
partialText: The New York Times is looking to talk to Jewish New Yorkers about whether their views on Israel and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict have changed.

title: N.Y.P.D. Fatally Shoots Man With Knife on Brooklyn Bridge
partialText: The shooting, on Friday morning, happened days after the police shot and killed a woman in Times Square who had stabbed two people.
